Shelves for a tidier desktop, and right-click on the Windows desktop.

**Shelves**
- A new kind of widget that holds desktop shortcuts and files. Each shelf shows a folder: `Documents/Desktop Shelves/<name>` by default, or any folder picked. Everything on it is an ordinary file there, so nothing is hidden away.
- **Three looks**, chosen per shelf: a frosted panel with snow piled on top (the default), a wooden shelf with snow on its planks, or a gift box with a gold ribbon and a bow.
- **Icons**, chosen per shelf: each item's real icon, or that icon redrawn as chunky pixel art. Items without an icon of their own get a little drawing of their type (folder, document, picture, music, video, archive, link, app).
- **Making one**: right-click (or press and hold) on the bare scene → *new shelf here*, or Settings → the new **Shelves** tab → *+ new shelf*. The tab renames shelves (their folder is renamed with them), changes their look and icons, opens their folder, and removes them (the files stay).
- **Using them**: double-click an item to open it. Long-press or right-click it for *open*, *show in its folder* and *take off the shelf*. Drag an item onto another shelf to move it there, or off the shelves to put it back on the desktop. Scroll with the wheel or the ▲ ▼ arrows. Click the title to roll the shelf up to one line, and drag the ◢ corner to resize it.
- **On Windows**: drag desktop icons straight onto a shelf to put them away, and drag them off to put them back on the desktop where they're let go. Moves go through Explorer, so Ctrl+Z on the desktop undoes them. Shortcuts on the shared "all users" desktop need admin rights to move, so they stay put.
- **On Linux**: apps open through KDE's launcher (or gio / xdg-open) in a systemd scope of their own, so they keep running when the wallpaper restarts. Real icons show in kitty through its graphics protocol.

**Right-click on the Windows desktop**
- Right-clicking someone in the village, an animal, a house, the station, the cabin, a widget or a shelf now opens its menu, as on Linux.
- On open ground, in the sky and on desktop icons it's still Windows' own desktop menu. Our menus have a *Windows desktop menu…* item too, and press-and-hold still opens our menu anywhere.
